task: Adopt the proven VX Publish Readiness Core in the active StorefrontVisualBuilderV3, enforce PASS-only publish enablement so UNKNOWN never behaves as PASS, preserve source/reason/localization/repairability presentation, and promote VX-PUBLISH-READINESS only after active-route executable proof.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The Publish Readiness Core is lifecycle-closed and proven, but the active StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 still uses a local Fidelity-only checklist. A preserved WIP adoption patch proved directionally useful but has a critical fail-closed defect: it allows publish while the canonical readiness decision is UNKNOWN. This wave must replace the active checklist with the canonical Core, present explainable evidence, and permit publish only when the aggregate decision is PASS. It must not create evidence producers, duplicate source authorities, change publish persistence, or infer repairs from pixel evidence.
observableOutcomes: The active admin Builder route continues to render StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 and that component consumes inspectStorefrontPublishReadiness.
The previous local Fidelity-only readiness array/status logic is removed from V3.
PASS, BLOCK and UNKNOWN are visibly distinct in the publish drawer.
Each displayed non-clean category exposes the Core-provided reason, authority/source, repairability and available localization.
Publish is enabled only when the canonical readiness decision is PASS, the draft is saved, and no busy state applies.
UNKNOWN blocks publish exactly like an unresolved proof state, without being relabeled as an error or PASS.
The UI does not generate repairs, mutate Page Schema from diagnostics, or convert pixel drift into a causal fix.
VX-PUBLISH-READINESS becomes PROVEN only after active V3 adoption and executable proof; Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix remain non-PROVEN.
Template #3 remains blocked because Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix remain mandatory unresolved capabilities.
unresolvedRisks: UI may display UNKNOWN but still leave the publish button enabled.
The active route could still render an older Builder component while tests inspect V3 only.
Presentation code could reconstruct a second readiness algorithm instead of consuming Core category states.
Warnings could be promoted to blockers or errors could be visually downgraded.
Pixel-only visual drift could be presented as a structured repair recommendation.
Maturity could be promoted from Core proof alone without proving active V3 adoption.
External evidence acquisition remains upstream; pages lacking required evidence must stay UNKNOWN and cannot publish.

in: Active StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 consumption of the proven storefront-publish-readiness Core.
PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN category presentation using Core outputs.
Explainable finding detail: reason, source authority, repairability and localization.
Active-route source proof that page.tsx renders V3 rather than legacy Builder surfaces.
Maturity promotion for VX-PUBLISH-READINESS only after executable UI adoption proof.
Regression proof that Smart Intent, Smart Auto-Fix and Template #3 remain blocked.
out: New visual, route, media, commerce or accessibility evidence producers.
Fetching CI artifacts from GitHub at runtime.
Page Schema mutation or Auto-Fix generation.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is the user-visible gate immediately adjacent to publishing. A false PASS or UNKNOWN-as-PASS would bypass the evidence contract. Highest practical assurance is active-route proof, fail-closed state-machine verification, source-level no-parallel-checklist checks, maturity separation and exact-head build/browser quality evidence without adding a new evidence authority.

acceptanceCriteria: The active Builder route imports/renders StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 and not StorefrontVisualBuilderProduction.
V3 imports and invokes inspectStorefrontPublishReadiness rather than rebuilding readiness categories locally.
V3 no longer contains the previous viewportStatus/readiness array/statusFromIssues checklist implementation.
The publish drawer renders Core category state and explainable finding details including authority/source and repairability.
The publish button is disabled whenever readiness.decision is BLOCK or UNKNOWN; only PASS may proceed.
Dirty/no-draft/busy conditions continue to block publish independently of readiness.
The V3 adoption does not pass invented external evidence or downgrade missing evidence; absent upstream proof remains UNKNOWN.
No pixel mismatch/hotspot is converted in V3 into a causal diagnosis, repair command or Builder mutation.
Production maturity promotes VX-PUBLISH-READINESS to PROVEN with canonical Core + active V3 + executable test evidence.
VX-SMART-INTENT and VX-SMART-AUTOFIX remain NOT_IMPLEMENTED and Template #3 remains not ready.
Release Risk stays within policy for this stacked transaction.
invariants: BLOCK dominates UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN dominates PASS inside the Core; V3 consumes, not redefines, that order.
Warnings remain source-authority warnings and do not become blockers unless the Core category state is BLOCK.
Readiness UI does not own publish persistence or domain truth.
External evidence acquisition is upstream; missing evidence cannot be fabricated in UI.
Full capability promotion requires both Core proof and active V3 adoption proof.

failureModes: Canonical decision is UNKNOWN but publish remains clickable.
V3 shows PASS because it independently recomputes only Fidelity checks.
A BLOCK category is rendered as a warning due presentation-only mapping.
The route test checks V3 source but the actual admin route still renders a legacy component.
Maturity becomes PROVEN without an active V3 implementation/test evidence row.
A visual pixel drift finding is rendered with an invented automatic repair instruction.
edgeCases: Dirty draft while readiness would otherwise PASS.
No draft revision while readiness would otherwise PASS.
Category with no findings but valid evidence.
Finding localized only by path/href and not nodeId.
Manual-review visual finding with no causal repairability.

alternatives.summary: Replace the active V3 checklist with direct consumption of the proven Core and enforce PASS-only publish.
alternatives.reason: Completes user-visible adoption without duplicating evidence authority.

alternatives.summary: Keep the Fidelity-only checklist and add more conditions.
alternatives.reason: Would preserve a parallel readiness authority and cannot express provenance or UNKNOWN correctly.

alternatives.summary: Make the admin UI fetch GitHub Actions evidence directly.
alternatives.reason: Would add external runtime coupling and a new evidence transport concern not required for this capability; missing upstream evidence must remain UNKNOWN.

specialistReviews.finding: The Core is already the canonical decision authority; V3 must be a presentation consumer only.
specialistReviews.resolution: Import the Core result and remove local readiness derivation.

specialistReviews.finding: The preserved WIP patch allows publish on UNKNOWN because it checks blockers only.
specialistReviews.resolution: Gate the action on readiness.decision==='PASS' in addition to existing busy/dirty/draft guards.

specialistReviews.finding: Tri-state readiness must stay understandable without turning UNKNOWN into an error.
specialistReviews.resolution: Render explicit PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN labels and Core reason/source/repairability details.

specialistReviews.finding: As a stacked transaction against the closed Core branch, expected material risk is admin-operations + builder-template-system only.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep scope to V3, maturity and tests; split again if additional substantive subsystem changes become necessary.

challenge.scenario: No external Visual Diff/media/commerce evidence exists.
challenge.resolution: V3 displays UNKNOWN and disables publish.

challenge.scenario: There are no BLOCK findings but one UNKNOWN category.
challenge.resolution: Button gating uses aggregate decision PASS, not blockers===0.

challenge.scenario: Core returns PASS with advisory warnings.
challenge.resolution: PASS decision remains publishable while warnings are displayed.

challenge.scenario: A pixel-only visual finding is manual-review.
challenge.finding: UI may be tempted to show a direct fix.
challenge.resolution: Display Core repairability only; no generated repair action.

challenge.scenario: Legacy component still contains old checklist helpers.
challenge.finding: Inactive source must not be mistaken for active authority.
challenge.resolution: Executable route-source proof targets page.tsx → StorefrontVisualBuilderV3.

challenge.scenario: Maturity promotion happens with Core evidence but no V3 test.
challenge.finding: Capability claim would be broader than proof.
challenge.resolution: PROVEN evidence requires Core implementation plus active V3 implementation and executable adoption test.

challenge.scenario: Core category findings arrive in a different order while category state is unchanged.
challenge.finding: Presentation must not infer a different decision from finding order or choose a lower-severity lead finding first.
challenge.resolution: V3 displays the Core category state as authority and selects explanatory lead evidence with BLOCK before UNKNOWN before advisory findings, without recomputing category truth.

challenge.scenario: Readiness decision is PASS with warnings, but the draft is dirty or no saved draft revision exists.
challenge.finding: Canonical readiness PASS cannot bypass existing draft-state preconditions for the publish action.
challenge.resolution: Publish remains disabled unless decision is PASS AND busy=false AND dirty=false AND draftRevision is present.

proofPlan: Plan Before Code and Release Risk projection on the stacked base.
Source proof that active page.tsx renders V3, not legacy production Builder.
UI source proof that old local readiness checklist is absent.
Adversarial UI proof that UNKNOWN disables publish and PASS can remain publishable with warnings.

Executable/source proof must show each non-clean V3 readiness category renders the Core-provided state plus finding reason, authority/source, repairability and any available page/viewport/node/path/href localization; removal of any one field must make the adoption regression test fail.
Source boundary proof that V3 does not fabricate external evidence or generate diagnostic mutations.
Maturity proof promotes only VX-PUBLISH-READINESS and leaves Smart Intent/Auto-Fix non-PROVEN.
Incremental Known Failure replay, Quality tests, TypeScript, production build, exact-head Template Factory proof, Completion Truth and lifecycle closure.

requirements.requirement: The active StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 consumes the canonical Publish Readiness Core and replaces the previous local checklist.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Active V3 cannot retain or recreate a separate Fidelity-only publish checklist.

requirements.requirement: V3 permits publish only when the canonical readiness decision is PASS; BLOCK and UNKNOWN both remain non-publishable.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: UNKNOWN can never enable the publish action.

requirements.requirement: VX-PUBLISH-READINESS is promoted only with Core plus active V3 executable evidence, while Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix remain non-PROVEN and Template #3 remains blocked.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Publish Readiness completion cannot promote Smart Intent, Smart Auto-Fix or Template #3 readiness.

notes: Eleventh Brabus hardening wave. The Publish Readiness Core is lifecycle-closed on parent HEAD a04d797f49bd8695d101d64ac7694773a984b184. This stacked wave exists because the combined Core+Admin change exceeded the main-branch Release Risk Budget; against the closed Core base, projected substantive risk is V3 admin adoption plus maturity metadata only. The preserved earlier WIP patch is not accepted as-is because it allowed publish on UNKNOWN. Template #3 remains forbidden until Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix are also PROVEN.
